newsitem.title: PERU: Fujimori's son cries for bodyguard slain in raid.
newsitem.headline: Fujimori's son cries for bodyguard slain in raid.

text.p: President Alberto Fujimori's son Kenji wept unconsolably on Thursday at the graveside of his bodyguard, slain while rescuing Peru's foreign minister from Marxist rebels at the Japanese ambassador's home.
"Your friend Kenji and all your friends in the Pachacutez command will always remember you as our friend," 16-year-old Kenji said before kissing the coffin of commando Juan Valer.

Standing at the shoulder of his father, Kenji cried openly as Peru's military buried Valer and Army Lt. Raul Jimenez, the only two commandos killed in Tuesday's assault which rescued all but one of the 72 hostages.
The president said he was indebted to Valer for teaching his son discipline and called the commando's death the "birth of a hero".
The Fujimori family's personal involvement in the four-month hostage standoff with Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels went deeper.
The president's mother and sister were among hundreds of captives released in the first hours after the Tupac Amaru rebels took more than 500 cocktail party guests hostage.
His brother Pedro was among the 71 hostages safely freed after 126 days in captivity. His daughter Keiko was his main source of personal solace during the first agonizing weeks of the crisis.
And Fujimori himself would almost certainly also have been captured at the cocktail party had he not been delayed arriving from a visit to the provinces.
